title: CLI arg parser (medium bed)
prompt:
Build a TypeScript module pair in the current directory:

1. src/arg-parser.ts — `parseArgs(argv: string[], spec)` where spec declares subcommands, each with flags ({ name, type: 'string'|'number'|'boolean', default?, required? }). Returns { subcommand, values, errors: string[] }. Rules: `--flag=value` and `--flag value` both work; booleans accept bare `--flag` (true) and `--no-flag` (false); unknown flags and missing required flags produce errors (never throw); a missing subcommand yields errors:['missing subcommand'].

2. src/config-merge.ts — `resolveConfig({ cliValues, fileConfig, envPrefix, env })`: precedence CLI > env > file > spec defaults. Env keys map FLAG_NAME (upper snake with the prefix, e.g. APP_MAX_RETRIES for maxRetries with prefix APP_). Type-coerce env strings per the spec type; a value that fails coercion produces an error entry, never a crash.

3. test/arg-parser.test.ts + test/config-merge.test.ts — node:test + node:assert/strict covering: both flag syntaxes, boolean negation, unknown/missing-required errors, full precedence chain (all four layers set for one flag), env coercion failure, and number coercion.

Run the tests with `node --test` (this Node runs .ts natively — do NOT use npx or install anything; the sandbox has no network) and make them all pass.

Acceptance command: node --test test/arg-parser.test.ts test/config-merge.test.ts
specification: CLI arg parser (medium bed) — the prompt is self-contained; build exactly what it asks in the current directory. Acceptance: `node --test test/arg-parser.test.ts test/config-merge.test.ts`.
